findings.title: Counting turns accumulated wealth into a permanence model
findings.claim: The focus's gathering of wealth and its subsequent counting can be read as a self-made accounting model in which a finite stock is treated as evidence of lasting security.
findings.mechanism: The gathering carrier takes wealth as its object and the coordinated counting verb repeatedly inventories that object; supplied comparisons with an estate expected never to perish and wealth unable to ransom its owner turn accumulation into a false inference about endurance.
findings.reader_payoff: The count becomes visible as an argument made by the possessor, not only as a description of possessions.
findings.containment: The plain reading remains the person who gathered wealth and counted it. This finding does not claim that counting is the sole motive or that wealth actually endures. The counted-limit comparison at 3:24 remains a non-wealth-specific counter-reading.

epistemic.reason: A citable trusted publication supplies exact focus branch anchors and a direct changed-reading claim; connection rows add bounded contextual corroboration without supplying target morphology.
